ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The side 1 on the left of the picture is a hexagon-shaped pattern enclosed by 6 identical small triangles, using 12 matches in total. The side 2 on the right only has a part drawn: the left slanted side already has 2 matches, there is a complete small triangle in the middle using 3 matches, and on the right side there is also 1 horizontally extending match, so 6 matches have already been drawn. Then reason: the complete side 2 figure is the same triangular-grid hexagon pattern, but each outer side has length 2 unit matches. This kind of triangular-grid hexagon with side length n contains 6n^2 small triangles, and the outer boundary has 6n unit edges. Each small triangle contributes 3 edges, but internal edges are shared by two triangles, so the total number of matches is (3·6n^2 + 6n)/2. Substituting n=2 gives (3·24 + 12)/2 = (72 + 12)/2 = 42 matches. The right-side part already has 6 matches, therefore 42 - 6 = 36 more matches are needed.

method.method_draft: Use a triangular-lattice edge count. From the image, first note that the completed figure is the same hexagon-made-of-triangles pattern as the side-1 figure on the left, but for side 2 each outer side has 2 unit matchsticks; the partial side-2 drawing on the right already shows 6 matchsticks: two on the left slanted side, three forming the small triangle, and one horizontal extension to the right. From the text, side 1 confirms the unit pattern: 6 equal triangles require 12 sticks. For a full hexagonal triangular grid of side length n, the number of small triangles is 6n^2 and the boundary has 6n unit edges; since each interior edge is shared by two triangles, total sticks are (3·6n^2 + 6n)/2. For n=2 this gives (72+12)/2 = 42 total sticks in the completed side-2 figure. Subtract the 6 sticks already shown in the partial drawing, so 42 - 6 = 36 matchsticks are needed to complete it.
